uvc_principles: UV-C 可损伤微生物 DNA/RNA 与部分幼体，抑制定殖或杀死早期生物膜。
船体应用面临：**水衰减、阴影、距离、LED 输出稳定性、聚合物/涂层光老化、功耗与密封**。
更现实的落点：niche 区（海箱、推进器隧道、传感器窗）、移动式/ROV 照射、嵌入式 LED 瓷砖试点——而非已验证的「整船外壳唯一方案」。
us_principles: 换能器在壳板激励振动/导波，干扰幼体附着或破坏早期生物膜；**预防优于清除**。
效果强烈依赖：**频率、功率、换能器间距与布局、壳板几何与阻尼、电源占空比**。
现场结果不一致：部分试验板洁净，部分商用系统对藤壶有抑制但对水线藻类/粘液/水螅类不足。

weeks.title: Industry Feed | 2026-11-23
weeks.coverage: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-23 (Beijing time; mainly the last 7 days, with international product news slightly widened to 14 days)
weeks.nature: Industry news / public sources, not performance data. Content drawn from the "Antifouling Industry Weekly", with dates and content checked against the original sources.
weeks.trend_summary: This week's theme is "biocide-free routes accelerating into products, biocide-containing routes accelerating into restriction": at METSTRADE, AkzoNobel launched Micron ReGen, a directly recoatable biocide-free yacht paint; Hempel backed an existing hybrid system with an independent life-cycle assessment; and GIT's graphene coating + robotic grooming produced a full year of in-service data — three lines that together point to hull performance management that does not rely on biocides moving from concept towards purchasable, applicable products and services. Meanwhile, the EU formally closed the medetomidine renewal with Decision (EU) 2026/2567 and set a market-exit line of 8 June 2027, in contrast with New Zealand's consultation in the previous issue: the access map for the same active substance is differentiating by jurisdiction. At the regulatory level, the nine shipping associations jointly called for global carbon rules, and with MEPC 85 and the resumed-session vote on 4 December approaching, every increment of hull resistance may translate directly into compliance cost — the shared economic backdrop for efficient antifouling and active hull management alike. On the domestic patent front, incremental routes such as silicone hybrids still predominate, with no comparable real-sea-level breakthrough seen.

entries.title: EU formally decides not to renew medetomidine (Selektope); countdown begins for antifouling paints containing the substance to exit the EU market
entries.summary: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2567, adopted by the European Commission on 19 November and published in the Official Journal on 20 November, formally does not renew the approval of medetomidine (trade name Selektope) as a biocidal active substance for product type 21 (antifouling products); the decision takes effect on 10 December 2026, and the accompanying Decision (EU) 2026/2566 simultaneously repeals the earlier extension that had prolonged the approval to 31 December 2026; from 8 June 2027, articles treated with, or intentionally incorporating, that substance may no longer be placed on the EU market. The decision rests on the European Chemicals Agency's May 2024 opinion concerning endocrine-disrupting properties: no safe exposure level could be established, nor could the risks of representative products be deemed acceptable. The decision also lists four chemical alternatives considered adequately available for commercial shipping and yachts: DCOIT, copper thiocyanate, cuprous oxide and tralopyril. Vessels already coated with Selektope coatings are unaffected and may continue to call at EU ports; I-Tech states that the EU market accounts for about 4% of its sales and that about 95% of the global commercial fleet can continue to use Selektope-containing coatings (company figures). This is the formal EU outcome following last issue's public consultation by the New Zealand EPA on the same active substance.
entries.relevance_reason: the split in Selektope access is now formally settled: the EU has closed the renewal by legislative decision and set a clear market-exit timetable, so the regional compliance risk for biocide-containing routes has shifted from "voting intention" to "decision in force", directly affecting the European market and formulation substitution choices for products containing this active substance
entries.note: Pending review (regional market-access wording for Selektope-containing products on the shortlist; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Jotun wins the coating contract for Knutsen's nine LNG newbuildings
entries.summary: On 18 November, Jotun announced it had won the contract to supply coatings for Knutsen's nine 174,000 m³ LNG carrier newbuildings, to be built by Hanwha Ocean in South Korea, with steel cutting starting in January 2027. The project selected Jotun Hull Performance Solutions (HPS 2.0), and the owner placed particular emphasis on antifouling technology and long-term coating performance in its bid evaluation; Jotun stressed its performance commitment across specification, construction and operation. This continues Jotun and Knutsen's multi-project cooperation at shipyards in Norway and South Korea.
entries.relevance_reason: a leading owner making antifouling technology and long-term hull performance a focus in bid evaluation for large LNG newbuildings confirms that "verifiable hull performance" has become an explicit criterion in newbuilding coating selection
entries.note: Pending review (shortlist narrative on the Jotun Hull Performance Solutions / SeaQuantum system; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Nine shipping associations jointly call for a global agreement on the IMO net-zero framework; MEPC 85 opens on 30 November
entries.summary: On 18 November, nine associations — BIMCO, CLIA, IBIA, ICS, INTERCARGO, INTERFERRY, INTERTANKO, IPTA and the World Shipping Council — issued a joint statement urging governments to reach "workable, enforceable and stable" global rules on the IMO net-zero framework, stressing that only global rules can avoid fragmentation of regional rules and double charging. MEPC 85 will be held in London from 30 November to 3 December, but an adoption vote is not on its agenda; the second extraordinary session, which adjourned in October 2025, is planned to resume on 4 December to vote on the MARPOL Annex VI amendments, and whether it resumes must first be confirmed by MEPC 85. The draft sets, for 2028–2030, two tiers of remedial-unit floor prices at USD 100 and USD 380 per tonne of CO₂ equivalent, and the entry-into-force date of 1 May 2028 remains in square brackets, undecided.
entries.relevance_reason: if global carbon pricing is implemented, it will directly raise the compliance cost of increased hull resistance, strengthening the economic value of efficient antifouling and hull performance management; but whether a vote can take place on 4 December is still uncertain, and the United States and other countries are clearly opposed

entries.title: Paper on a fluorine-free laser superhydrophobic coating published: femtosecond laser + point-like organic–inorganic reinforcement
entries.summary: A study published in Progress in Organic Coatings (article 110466): 7075 aluminium alloy was textured by femtosecond laser into a biomimetic cauliflower-like multi-scale structure; KH550 silane formed an Al-O-Si interfacial anchoring layer; KH570-modified ZnO and low-solids E44 epoxy built a point-like reinforcing skeleton; and octadecyltrimethoxysilane provided the low-surface-energy outer layer, with no fluorinated modifiers used anywhere in the process. The optimised coating had a water contact angle of 163.4° and a sliding angle of 2.1°, remained superhydrophobic after 240 abrasion cycles and 200 tape-peeling cycles, achieved an anticorrosion efficiency of 99.86% after 100 hours of immersion in 3.5% NaCl (by electrochemical impedance), delayed icing at −20 °C from 181 seconds to 857 seconds, and reduced ice adhesion strength from 142 kPa to 34 kPa. Antifouling is only a potential application direction; no marine organism attachment tests were carried out.
entries.relevance_reason: the durability thinking behind fluorine-free superhydrophobic interfaces is relevant to antifouling surface design, but the subject is a laboratory aluminium-alloy specimen with no real-sea antifouling evidence, indirectly related to hull antifouling formulation selection

entries.title: Neptune Robotics partners with Louis Dreyfus to trial AI hull-cleaning robots in Singapore
entries.summary: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC) and Neptune Robotics have entered a partnership to run robotic hull-cleaning trials under the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) innovation programme for underwater hull inspection and cleaning, lasting 18 months; LDC will open its fleet of more than 300 chartered vessels for in-service testing, evaluating the inspection and cleaning performance of the AI-driven robots and their impact on fuel consumption and emissions, with results expected in 2028. Neptune's MAGNETO robot uses cavitation water jets to remove hull fouling; the company states it can clean a fully laden Capesize vessel within 24 hours, operate in currents of 4 knots, and does not damage the underlying antifouling coating while recovering the removed material; the operating capabilities above are company-stated, and trial results have not yet been produced.
entries.relevance_reason: after Cargill, a second major charterer joins the MPA robotic cleaning trials; hull cleaning is shifting from an emergency port service to routine management with a data loop, directly affecting how cleanable antifouling systems are maintained in service
entries.note: Pending review (shortlist wording on hull-cleaning compatibility; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: AkzoNobel's International brand launches biocide-free yacht antifouling Micron ReGen
entries.summary: On 17 November at METSTRADE, AkzoNobel launched Micron ReGen under its International brand, described as the first yacht antifouling to use "Surface Renewal Technology": a microporous surface layer with both hydrophilic and hydrophobic character continuously renews the surface after immersion to hinder attachment, with no biocide required. The company states that three seasons of in-service trials showed fuel savings of 4.7% and a speed increase of 1.7% at equal power (company-stated trial data, with no independent verification seen); it can be brushed or rolled directly over old antifouling in good condition (except PTFE types), with no primer or tie coat needed, and the vessel can be launched the same day it is applied; it initially goes on sale in 11 European markets — the United Kingdom, Ireland, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Austria and Switzerland — in a total of 5 colours.
entries.relevance_reason: the biocide-free route gains a directly recoatable new product aimed at the yacht market, with an application threshold clearly lower than that of existing biocide-free systems; the performance figures are company-stated and need independent data support
entries.note: Pending review (shortlist wording on biocide-free routes and recoat compatibility; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Chinese patent published for a low-migration siloxane-grafted acrylic antifouling coating
entries.summary: On 17 November, the China National Intellectual Property Administration published an antifouling coating invention patent (applicant: Luo Juan): a di-epoxy-terminated siloxane is prepared by hydrosilylation and reacted with an aminosilane to obtain a "self-anchoring siloxane", which is then copolymerised with acrylates to give a siloxane-grafted acrylic resin; its design goal is to chemically anchor the siloxane segments within the resin network, reducing the loss of low surface energy caused by silicone oil migrating to the coating surface, while the acrylic resin provides adhesion and mechanical strength. A patent publication is only a disclosure of a technical solution, with no real-sea antifouling validation data.
entries.relevance_reason: a domestic patent development on the silicone–acrylic hybrid route, related to low-surface-energy antifouling formulation thinking, but it is only a patent publication, with no performance or real-sea evidence

entries.title: GIT graphene foul-release coating + onboard robotic grooming completes one year of in-service operation
entries.summary: An industry analysis published on 15 November reviewed a case disclosed by GIT Coatings: a gas carrier using a graphene-based foul-release coating, together with an onboard robotic grooming system, completed a full year of continuous commercial operation, during which 7 underwater inspections and 3 grooming sessions were carried out; according to GIT's disclosure, power performance after dry-docking improved by about 6% against the previous premium antifouling baseline, added power growth over the year was kept within about 2% (including more than 180 days idle), each grooming session restored 3–5% efficiency, and no hard fouling appeared over the year and the coating showed no measurable degradation. All of these figures are from a single-vessel case disclosed by the company and have not been independently verified by a third party; the underlying case study was reported at the HullPIC conference in early 2026. BW Epic Kosan has expanded its adoption of the system across multiple LPG carriers.
entries.relevance_reason: the "continuous hull management" model of biocide-free coating + active grooming now has its first full year of in-service data, but it is a single vessel with company-stated figures, and multi-vessel, multi-year data with independent verification is needed before it can serve as a basis for selection

entries.title: Hempel showcases Hempaguard X7 at METSTRADE, with independent life-cycle assessment data
entries.summary: At the METSTRADE show in Amsterdam on 17–19 November, Hempel included Hempaguard X7 in its superyacht sustainability route (booth 02.423) and cited a comparative life-cycle assessment by the Water Revolution Foundation: compared with the conventional Hempel Mille NCT 71880 scheme, endpoint-level environmental impact improved by 31.5% (this figure is an aggregated indicator under the specific assumptions of that assessment, not a fuel-saving rate, and cannot be read directly as fuel savings). Hempaguard X7 is not itself a new product (Hempel launched it in 2013); it is a hybrid system of a silicone hydrogel surface plus an antifouling biocide, not a biocide-free coating; its selling point is the independent assessment evidence for superyacht duty involving long idle periods.
entries.relevance_reason: life-cycle evidence for biocide-free / low-impact routes is entering yacht selection discussions, but the product itself contains a biocide and is not new, and the 31.5% is an assessment figure rather than measured fuel savings

weeks.title: Industry Feed | 2026-11-16
weeks.coverage: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-16 (Beijing time; mainly the last 7 days, with international product/company news slightly widened to 14 days)
weeks.nature: Industry news / public sources, not performance data. Content drawn from the "Antifouling Industry Weekly", with dates and content checked against the original sources.
weeks.trend_summary: This week, Selektope access diverged: after EU member states voted to support non-renewal, New Zealand's EPA promptly opened a public consultation on the substance and on yacht paints containing it, making the direction of regional access a key variable for biocide-containing routes. On the copper-free side, the papers on the oyster-shell bio-based coating and the kaolin superhydrophobic coating both offered laboratory highlights alongside explicit caveats at the real-sea and mechanism levels, a reminder that formulation selection should still be governed by real-sea evidence. On the supply side, coating automation landed in a concentrated way across domestic shipyards — laser cleaning equipment released, four-robot linked painting, electrostatic spraying entering dry-dock repair — which, together with Jotun's DNV-verified data, pushes "verifiable hull performance" to the fore; leading manufacturers' group results continued to grow, and domestic package orders expanded in step.

entries.title: CSSC Shuangrui brand day: contract signed for a coating package order for 5 × 109,000-tonne crude oil tankers
entries.summary: On 13 November, the "Entering CSSC Shuangrui" event of the 2026 CSSC series brand days was held in Luoyang; the "Shuangrui" brand is valued at RMB 8.444 billion, with a brand strength of 945, rising for ten consecutive years; six technical reports covered directions including integrated corrosion and antifouling protection; six categories of projects were signed on site, including real-ship application orders such as the coating package for 5 × 109,000-tonne crude oil tankers; Shuangrui is the civilian-products brand of CSSC's 725th Research Institute, backed by the National Key Laboratory of Marine Corrosion and Protection.

entries.title: Multiple domestic shipyards accelerate their green, intelligent coating transformation
entries.summary: The China Association of the National Shipbuilding Industry summarised green, intelligent coating practices at several shipyards: Zhoushan COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry has put into use ultra-high-pressure water rust-removal boom vehicles (reportedly with a maximum working height of 28 m and single-unit efficiency of up to 120 m²/h), China's first intelligent coating platform for green ship repair and building (maximum working height 35.5 m, millimetre-level spraying precision) and a digital energy-and-carbon management centre; Hudong-Zhonghua carried out real-ship trials of portable, domestically made automated shot-blasting robots on a general-assembly block of the 13,600 TEU vessel H1947A (unit weight 28 kg; one operator can control two units simultaneously); GSI ran four painting robots in linked operation for the first time; and Shanghai COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry, during a dry-dock repair of a Jotun-coated vessel, used a silicone coating for the first time and applied PPG SIGMAGLIDE® 2390 by electrostatic spraying, with the company stating that coating utilisation rose by 30% and paint consumption fell by 15%–30% compared with traditional airless spraying.
entries.relevance_reason: coating automation and low-VOC processes are landing in a concentrated way across domestic shipyards, and the electrostatic spraying + silicone foul-release combination has entered real-ship dry-dock repair, benchmarkable against application-process wording on the shortlist

entries.title: Nippon Paint Holdings posts record Q3: revenue and adjusted operating profit both increase

entries.title: Paper on a kaolin-reinforced superhydrophobic epoxy anticorrosion coating published
entries.summary: The November 2026 issue of Coatings (vol. 16, issue 11, article 1339) published a study of a three-layer superhydrophobic anticorrosion coating: a kaolin-reinforced epoxy primer + elastic adhesive interlayer + hydrophobic SiO₂ topcoat, with a water contact angle of 157.8° and a sliding angle of 2.1°; superhydrophobicity was retained after 19 m of abrasion or 200 tape-peeling cycles; in 3.5% NaCl, the corrosion current density fell to 7.9×10⁻¹² A·cm⁻², with a protection efficiency of about 99.33% after 15 days of immersion; the structure remained intact through salt-spray, immersion, outdoor and UV-ageing tests and antifouling self-cleaning tests; the antifouling evidence was only a qualitative laboratory self-cleaning test, with no real-sea antifouling validation.
entries.relevance_reason: mainly anticorrosion and self-cleaning interface design; the antifouling evidence is limited to qualitative laboratory tests, indirectly related to hull antifouling formulation selection

entries.title: New Zealand EPA opens public consultation on Selektope imports and Selektope-containing yacht paint
entries.summary: On 5 November, the New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) opened public consultations on two applications, closing on 17 December: I-Tech's application to import or manufacture the new active substance Selektope (medetomidine) (APP204449), and Altex Coatings' application for its Altex Ablative Antifoul (TFS) range of antifouling paints containing that substance (APP204450). If approved, Selektope would be limited to professional use in commercial settings for manufacturing antifouling paint, while the finished paints are intended for both professional and non-professional users; the EPA will assess the human-health and New Zealand environmental risks and benefits. This is Selektope's market-access progress in another jurisdiction after EU member states voted on 3 November to support non-renewal.
entries.relevance_reason: the direction of Selektope access in New Zealand after its setback in the EU directly affects regional market expectations for products containing this active substance
entries.note: Pending review (regional market-access wording for Selektope-containing products on the shortlist; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: GSI releases world-first dual high-pulse laser cleaning equipment
entries.summary: On 5 November, CSSC Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI), together with the Qilu Zhongke Institute of Optical Physics and Engineering Technology and Beijing Xinshuanggao Technology, released in Nansha a new generation of dual high-nanosecond pulsed laser cleaning equipment; the 3 kW and 4 kW single-cavity single-mode models are world firsts, filling a domestic gap in efficient, intelligent pulsed laser cleaning equipment for ship repair and building; a 4,000 W high-power wall-climbing robot laser cleaning system was demonstrated on site; the company states the equipment produces little dust and low noise and is highly intelligent; GSI is also leading the development of a group standard, "Technical Requirements for Laser Cleaning Before Ship Coating".
entries.relevance_reason: new automation equipment for pre-coating surface preparation, concerning rust-removal efficiency and the basis for coating adhesion, but it belongs to the pre-treatment stage rather than to antifouling formulation itself

entries.title: Paper on an oyster-shell bio-based dual-temperature antifouling coating published
entries.summary: The November 2026 issue of Coatings (vol. 16, issue 11, article 1304) published a study by a Taiwanese team: a waterborne acrylic coating combining oyster shell powder calcined at 600 °C (15 wt% of dry solids) with AZO@SiO₂ core–shell nanoparticles; in 12-month real-sea panel immersion at Anping Port, macrofouling was visibly lower than on the blank control, though local deposition remained; under 100 W/m² laboratory illumination, the coating surface rose to 42.1±1.8 °C within 90 seconds (control 31.2±0.8 °C); in a 28-day leaching test, Cu, Zn, Sn and Fe were all below detection limits; the volatile-amine repellence and photothermal antifouling mechanisms remain hypotheses, and the authors explicitly did not carry out controlled attachment-biology validation.
entries.relevance_reason: a copper-free waterborne antifouling idea based on waste valorisation, benchmarkable against biocide-free formulation routes; the unverified mechanism and limited real-sea effect are important caveats

entries.title: Jotun publishes DNV-verified data from its PortPIC 2026 study
entries.summary: On 2 November, Jotun released the verified-data basis of its PortPIC 2026 study (the underlying article was published on 26 October and was covered in the previous issue): based on the ISO 19030 method and real-ship operating data, DNV verified, across 33 vessels using Hull Skating Solutions, an average of 3.5 years with no measurable speed loss and hulls kept always clean; one large container ship cut CO₂ by 17.7% per year, about 17,300 tonnes. A second study showed that controlled surface treatment and application of sea chests can improve antifouling performance. The study also accounted for the footprint of the coating, the robot and the onboard station itself, concluding that the net climate benefit is positive. The emission-reduction figures above are company figures on a DNV verification basis, not measurements made by this simulator.
entries.relevance_reason: DNV third-party-verified, whole-ship-level data on active cleaning + coating directly affects the selection of cleanable antifouling systems and hull performance
entries.note: Pending review (shortlist narrative on Hull Skating-compatible systems such as Jotun SeaQuantum; ratings unchanged)

weeks.nature: Industry news / public sources, not performance data. Content drawn from the "Antifouling Industry Weekly", with dates and content checked against the original sources.
weeks.trend_summary: Robotic cleaning has entered the real-ship validation stage with major shipowners: the Cargill–Neptune Singapore trial ties cleaning efficiency, coating compatibility and measured fuel savings together. The EU non-renewal of Selektope and California's siloxane restrictions tighten, on two fronts, the compliance space for biocide-containing and silicone routes; the copper-free bio-based coating paper shows there is still a gap between laboratory algae inhibition and real-sea performance. Leading manufacturers' marine coating volumes continue to grow and domestic package certifications expand — the next stage will look more at measured cleaning data, regional market-access changes for products containing active substances, and real-sea evidence for copper-free formulations.

entries.title: Southern California SCAQMD proposes amending Rule 1106 to tighten VOC and siloxanes in marine coatings
entries.summary: The South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD) in Southern California has issued a CEQA exemption notice for amending Rule 1106 on marine and pleasure-craft coatings: it proposes phasing out coatings containing more than trace amounts of parachlorobenzotrifluoride (pCBtF) and tert-butyl acetate (t-BAc), prohibiting the sale and use of coatings containing more than trace amounts of fully methylated siloxanes, and adding VOC limits together with record-keeping and labelling requirements; the expected reduction is 23.9 pounds of VOC per day.
entries.relevance_reason: methylated-siloxane restrictions directly touch silicone foul-release coating formulations, and tighter VOC rules affect solvent-borne systems

entries.title: EU member states support non-renewal of the Selektope (medetomidine) approval
entries.summary: EU member states voted to support the European Commission's proposal not to renew the approval of Selektope (active substance medetomidine) as a PT21 antifouling biocide; once the formal decision is published, a transition period of about 180 days is expected, during which Selektope-containing coatings may still be supplied and applied in the EU, after which they may no longer be placed on the EU market; vessels already coated are unaffected. I-Tech states that about 95% of the global commercial fleet can continue to use it, that its direct EU exposure is about 4% of its revenue, and that it will object through scientific, regulatory and legal channels.
entries.relevance_reason: directly affects EU market access for Selektope-containing commercial antifouling paints, favouring tracking of biocide-free routes
entries.note: Pending review (EU market-access wording for Selektope-containing products such as CMP Sea Premier in the shortlist / commercial-products.md; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Cargill × Neptune Robotics robotic hull-cleaning trial in Singapore
entries.summary: Cargill and Neptune Robotics have launched an 18-month collaboration under the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) innovation programme for underwater hull inspection and cleaning, using an AI remotely operated cleaning robot (the flagship MAGNETO) to clean and inspect Cargill's calling vessels underwater, with before-and-after performance comparisons to calculate fuel savings; the company states its system can clean a fully laden Capesize vessel within 24 hours and covers 61 ports in Singapore and China; the fuel-saving results have not yet been published and remain to be measured in practice.
entries.relevance_reason: a major shipowner's real-ship validation of robotic cleaning and coating compatibility directly affects the selection of cleanable antifouling systems

entries.title: Beixin Lighthouse: 14 marine coatings certified by CCS
entries.summary: Fourteen new marine coating products from Beixin Lighthouse have completed China Classification Society (CCS) certification, covering three scenarios — hull corrosion protection, oil tanks and cargo holds — including the low-surface-treatment epoxy paint DC-H950D, the alkyd primer/finish-in-one paint DC-C40Y and the high-build epoxy micaceous iron oxide paint DC-H500Z; the company states that its full product line complies with IMO environmental standards, focusing on high-solids and solvent-free formulations.
entries.relevance_reason: expansion of domestic marine coating package capability, benchmarkable against domestic systems on the shortlist
entries.note: Pending review (Beixin Lighthouse products are not yet in the database; whether to include them in commercial-products.md is undecided; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Nippon Paint India launches low-zinc shop primer NIPPON CERAMO
entries.summary: Nippon Paint India is introducing the low-zinc inorganic shop primer NIPPON CERAMO to the Indian marine coatings market, for protecting steel before fabrication; the company states it can withstand 800 °C, reduces welding and cutting damage and zinc fume generation, and holds relevant compliance documentation under IMO MSC.215(82)/MSC.288(87); it is the company's entry point into the Indian marine coatings business.
entries.relevance_reason: shop primers belong to the shipbuilding pre-treatment stage, indirectly related to hull antifouling formulation selection

entries.title: Paper on a bio-based amphiphilic polymer antifouling coating published
entries.summary: The November 2026 issue of Marine Pollution Bulletin (vol. 232, article 120083) published a study of a bio-based amphiphilic polymer antifouling coating: the coating was prepared from renewable platform chemicals by free-radical polymerisation that avoids harmful solvents, tuning the hydrophilic/hydrophobic balance; in laboratory tests, the hydrophobe-dominant formulation inhibited diatom attachment by more than 90% and showed no detectable acute toxicity to Artemia; however, in static real-sea panel immersion the amphiphilic formulations failed to prevent fouling accumulation, indicating that further optimisation is still needed. Only the publication month (November 2026) is known; the exact online date has not been announced.
entries.relevance_reason: design ideas for copper-free bio-based antifouling binders, benchmarkable against biocide-free formulation routes; the shortfall in real-sea performance is an important caveat

entries.title: PPG Q3 2026: high-single-digit organic sales growth in protective and marine coatings
entries.summary: PPG released its Q3 2026 results, with group net sales of USD 4.353 billion (up 7% year on year); organic sales in protective and marine coatings grew at a high single-digit rate year on year, achieving the 14th consecutive quarter of volume growth, with marine coating volumes in Asia-Pacific growing faster than the market.
entries.relevance_reason: demand-side momentum in marine coatings at a leading manufacturer, benchmarkable against the SIGMAGLIDE / NEXEON promotion pace
entries.note: Pending review (shortlist PPG SIGMAGLIDE 2390 and NEXEON promotional claims; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Roundup of antifouling keynote reports at the Qingdao marine corrosion protection conference

entries.title: POC: copper-free acrylic antifouling binder with covalently grafted QSI
entries.summary: Dewas et al. covalently incorporated a quorum-sensing inhibitor (QSI) into an acrylic binder to build a copper-free antifouling paint; the abstract reports that biomass in a seawater trial of about six months was lower than that of the unmodified control.
entries.relevance_reason: copper-free, non-traditional biocide release pathways and binder molecular design can be directly benchmarked against formulation routes

entries.title: Dewei solvent-free high-solids G50/G60/G80 and underwater cleaning robot

entries.note: Pending review (Dewei G60 etc. not yet in the database; whether to include them in commercial-products.md / the shortlist is undecided; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Jotun at PortPIC: Hull Skating climate footprint and sea-chest antifouling application
entries.summary: The installation footprint of Hull Skating (coating + robot) is about 423 t CO₂, and about 2,036 t over 25 years; against this, the DNV-verified avoided emissions under an always-clean-hull scenario are far higher than the footprint; controlled treatment of sea chests can significantly reduce fouling.

entries.note: Pending review (commercial-products.md / shortlist narrative on Hull Skating-compatible systems such as Jotun SeaQuantum; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Trosvik MultiCleaner ROV: R&D launched targeting zero untreated discharge

entries.title: MIIT implementation plan for dual control of carbon emissions in the industrial and information-technology fields (2026–2030)

entries.title: Propspeed Foulfree Multi-Surface wins IBEX Innovation Award

entries.relevance_reason: yacht accessories segment, indirectly related to commercial-ship hull formulation selection

entries.title: PPG RightShip interview: SIGMAGLIDE 2390 / NEXEON 810 + HullNav

entries.title: Ministry of Ecology and Environment "China's Policies and Actions for Addressing Climate Change — 2026 Annual Report"
entries.summary: Emphasises expansion of the national carbon market and progress in product carbon-footprint accounting, labelling and certification, and the development of application scenarios.

entries.title: Shuangrui completes the coating package for a batch of four 18,500 DWT oil/chemical tankers
entries.summary: For a batch of four oil/chemical tankers built by Fujian Shipbuilding's Southeast Shipyard for Intercontinental Shipping, Shuangrui supplied the coating package and on-site service; the fourth vessel, DN517-12, has been launched, wrapping up the series. The focus is cargo-tank corrosion protection for chemical tankers; no antifouling performance data was disclosed.
entries.relevance_reason: progress in domestic marine coating packages, indirectly related to antifouling formulation selection

entries.title: Fleet Robotics magnetic-adhesion stepping hull-cleaning robot (preventive maintenance at sea)
entries.summary: A magnetic-foot stepping cleaning robot can be permanently carried aboard a vessel, brush the hull autonomously at sea and return to its dock to recharge; it has been tested on a real vessel at WHOI. The report cautions that overly frequent cleaning may damage coatings.
entries.relevance_reason: affects how cleanable foul-release / silicone coatings fit active-cleaning routes, and their abrasion-resistance design

entries.title: POC: hydrodynamic stability window of a xanthan-gum hydrogel coating and field copper reduction
entries.summary: OCT + CFD converted rotor shear into an equivalent ship speed; the hydrogel thinned gradually at an equivalent speed of about 7 knots; xanthan gum with particle size <32 μm could reduce Cu₂O from 10 wt% to 6 wt% while achieving comparable field antifouling performance.
entries.relevance_reason: low-copper self-polishing formulations and hydrogel-layer stability within the service-speed window

entries.title: US EPA approves label amendment for Sea Hawk AF33 copper-based antifouling paint
entries.summary: Implements the label mitigation measures from the copper compounds registration review interim decision; old labels must be replaced with new ones after a 12-month transition period.
entries.relevance_reason: US regulation of copper-based yacht antifouling continues to tighten, favouring low-copper / copper-free routes
entries.note: Pending review (evidence basis for the copper-based SPC shortlist (Sea Hawk is not in the database, but tighter copper regulation affects the shortlist basis); ratings unchanged)

entries.title: POC: GARField NMR non-destructively characterises CuPy release in PDMS
entries.summary: 1D ¹H NMR profiles tracked the diffusion-controlled release front of CuPy in opaque antifouling coatings, cross-checked against SEM; reliable detection is possible above about 15 wt%, making the method suitable for formulation screening.
entries.relevance_reason: a release-kinetics characterisation method that can be borrowed for evaluating biocide / functional-component release

entries.title: CPC Central Committee and State Council "Opinions on Developing New Quality Productive Forces"

entries.title: Ministry of Transport "Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Pollution of the Marine Environment by Ships and Their Related Operations" (2026 revision)
entries.summary: Effective from 2026-11-01; ship materials must comply with antifouling inspection specifications, bunkering of new fuels is brought under supervision, and outboard painting work in port areas must be reported.
entries.relevance_reason: tighter compliance wording for coating application and materials, affecting real-ship application and inspection liaison

entries.title: Marine Industry News: fragmented regional regulation drives demand for biocide-free foul-release
entries.summary: EU biocide rules and North American state-level copper/VOC limits have fragmented product availability, and the yacht segment is accelerating biocide-free foul-release and regionally tailored formulations.
entries.relevance_reason: affects biocide-free product selection for cross-regional routes
entries.note: Pending review (commercial-products.md / shortlist FRC entries such as International Intersleek; ratings unchanged)

entries.title: Biofouling: dual-site field sea trial (Florida estuary and ocean) of UVC combined with marine coatings
entries.summary: Fouling was heavier in the turbid estuary and turbidity attenuated the UVC; at the ocean site, 9-month panels showed UVC could suppress macrofouling on four coatings; silicone was the most chemically sensitive to UVC, but the overall impact was limited.
entries.relevance_reason: directly relevant to UV-C / coating synergistic antifouling, turbidity zoning and duty-cycle design

weeks.title: Industry Feed | 2026-10-19
weeks.nature: Industry news / public sources, not performance data. Content drawn from the "Antifouling Industry Weekly"; all items checked against the original sources for date and content.
weeks.trend_summary: IMO convention discussion is shifting from "whether to capture" to "how to measure and how to prove it", and China is likewise developing a group standard for accelerated assessment methods for long-life antifouling coatings. The biocide-free route advanced on both the product and technology-licensing fronts. New evidence that bacteria are generally copper-tolerant weakens the long-term outlook for copper-based antifoulants, and research into stimulus-responsive, low-release formulations continued to heat up.

entries.title: Nippon Paint marine coatings exhibits its biocide-free AFC coating at the Fujian maritime expo and signs a joint research agreement with South China University of Technology
entries.summary: Nippon Paint calls its Advanced Fouling Control (AFC) coating the "world's first product containing no biocidal inhibitor", and has signed an industry–university–research project on "joint development of advanced antifouling coating technology" with South China University of Technology.
entries.relevance_reason: a candidate commercial biocide-free option, but performance data have not yet been made public

entries.title: Guangdong Zhongke Yuanhang underwater cleaning robot makes its first appearance at the World Maritime Equipment Conference
entries.summary: Stated cleaning efficiency of about 800 m²/h and a maximum working depth of 500 m, with brush-disc and cavitation water-jet modes; it is currently controlled manually by joystick, and reports mention no debris-capture function.
entries.relevance_reason: cleaning equipment; indirectly related to formulation choice

entries.title: Chemical Engineering Journal: light-responsive microcapsule on-demand antifouling coating inspired by fluorescent corals
entries.summary: Microcapsules of eugenol, SiO₂/TiO₂ and long-afterglow phosphor are embedded in polyurea-modified PDMS, releasing faster under strong light and losing less under weak light; reported antibacterial rates of 98–99%, anti-diatom rates of 75–80% and a thermal self-healing efficiency of 93.3%.
entries.relevance_reason: stimulus-responsive release and the PDMS system are of reference value for formulation design, and relate to routes differentiated by light intensity

entries.title: China Coatings Industry Association group standard "Accelerated assessment method for the antifouling performance of high-performance long-life antifouling coatings" launched online on October 23
entries.summary: The standard was proposed by the 725th Research Institute and initiated in October 2024 (CNCIA-2024-1003); the launch and first discussion meeting was held online on October 23, 14:00–16:00.
entries.relevance_reason: directly concerns accelerated assessment methods for formulation antifouling performance and domestic evaluation criteria

entries.title: I-Tech obtains an exclusive global aquaculture licence for Titanium Technology's electrochemical titanium-surface antifouling technology
entries.summary: Controlled electrochemical conditions created on a titanium surface inhibit initial biofilm formation, without biocides, coatings or chemical release; it is still an early-stage project, and commercial-scale application on nets/cages has not yet been verified.
entries.relevance_reason: aimed at aquaculture, a non-coating route, with limited impact on ship formulations and route selection

entries.title: The merged AkzoNobel and Axalta company is to be named Axanzo

entries.summary: After two weeks of panel immersion in Chesapeake Bay, the bacteria on uncoated control panels were as copper-tolerant as those on copper-coated panels, able to grow at copper concentrations above 70 mg/L (the EPA short-term seawater limit is 18 μg/L).
entries.relevance_reason: directly concerns the long-term effectiveness of copper-based antifoulants against microbial films
entries.note: Pending review (evidence basis for the copper-based SPC shortlist; rating unchanged)

entries.title: PortPIC conference review: as the IMO convention nears, in-water cleaning enters the "verifiable" stage
entries.summary: Capture is expected to be written into future rules, but the capture proportion, particle size, measurement approach and verification method are still undecided; a pilot at the Port of Bergen with DNV and NIVA proposed a benchmark of ≥80% capture and separation efficiency, and the BRADD project will provide data to IMO PPR by 2027.

entries.title: Review: AI and machine learning for designing sustainable marine antifouling coatings

Elsawy of Al-Azhar University, published in the Journal of Materials Science: Polymers, discusses using AI/ML to break the "trial-and-error" mode of antifouling formulation development, and identifies inconsistent data, a lack of standardised testing and a lack of long-term real-sea data as the main bottlenecks.

entries.title: Yutong Paint self-polishing system serves 26 months on an Aframax tanker on the Asia–Europe–Arctic route
entries.summary: The 100,000-tonne-class tanker was recoated in July 2024 with Yutep876 epoxy anti-abrasion paint and Yutaf933S6 Plus self-polishing antifouling paint; when it drydocked in September 2026, the fouling rate and corrosion rate were both 1% (versus 80% and 10% respectively at the previous drydocking); the figures are company-stated.

entries.summary: Hyperbranched polycaprolactone chemically crosslinked with an isothiazolinone-functionalised amphiphilic polymer achieves anti-adhesion, controlled biocide release and controlled degradation simultaneously; compared with physical blending, cumulative biocide release fell to about 1/20.
entries.relevance_reason: a formulation strategy of chemically anchoring the biocide to reduce release

entries.title: Sunrui silicone antifouling paint completes the National Day drydock application on the "Huahaihang 3"
entries.summary: The product relies mainly on low surface energy for physical antifouling; reports say it can save about 5%–12% of fuel over the full life cycle and cut overall coating cost by about 30%–40%; the figures are as reported in the coverage and have not been independently verified.

entries.title: UCIBIO: marinone-type natural-product biocide-free coating reduces mussel settlement

entries.title: New Zealand MPI commissions LWP to survey shipowners' views on biocide-free antifouling

entries.relevance_reason: could influence New Zealand's policy stance toward biocide-free coatings

entries.title: Biofouling: two panel stations on Florida's east coast evaluate the antifouling performance of UV-C combined with coatings
entries.summary: The Center for Corrosion and Biofouling Control at Florida Institute of Technology (Yeshi, Hunsucker et al.) compared the antifouling performance of UV-C combined with ship coatings (information from Crossref metadata; the full journal text was not opened).

entries.summary: Five LPG carriers have been coated so far (with one more in dock). entries.summary: DNV assessed underwater inspection data from 33 vessels and performance monitoring from 12 vessels over an average of 3.5 years (per ISO 19030, including a 1-year baseline period), confirming that hulls using HSS remained essentially free of fouling with no measurable speed loss over the observation period.

entries.title: 725th Research Institute completes silicone biomimetic drag-reduction antifouling coating on "Rui Lu Hao"
entries.summary: The vessel trades along China's southern, eastern and northern coasts and left dock in early May; the report stresses that nutrient-rich nearshore waters and long low-speed berthing mean both fouling pressure and coating wear are higher than in ocean service, and this application is seen as a validation of silicone biomimetic coatings on high-frequency nearshore vessels.

entries.title: Xinhe Wuxi self-polishing antifouling paint used in dry-dock repair of a 114,000-tonne Aframax tanker
entries.summary: The docking lasted only 4 days, overlapping with cross-trades work such as welding and plate renewal; the company states the product suits high-pressure airless spraying, cures quickly, has a controllable hydrolysis rate and is tin-free. The above is company-stated.
entries.relevance_reason: a full-scale application case for a domestic tin-free SPC, a useful reference for short-docking scenarios

entries.title: Quebec PAINTS project: multi-site panel testing of biocide-free xerogel and silicone coatings
entries.summary: Research teams in Quebec and France tested 8 xerogel and silicone coatings at sites including Rimouski, Sept-Îles, Toulon, Lorient and Réunion; some biocide-free coatings performed slightly worse than biocide-containing paints but showed real antifouling effect and are environmentally safe, durability still needs improvement, and they are not yet at the stage of large-scale commercialisation.
entries.relevance_reason: comparisons across waters from cold to tropical; a reference for the regional applicability of biocide-free formulations

entries.title: I-Tech releases barnacle fouling risk white paper: coating selection is a key risk factor
entries.summary: The white paper is based on Safinah Group dry-dock inspection data: of 686 vessels, more than one third entered dock with barnacle coverage above 10%, and nearly one fifth above 20%; fouling-release coatings are more prone to barnacle settlement during long idle periods, in warm water and low-speed service, and at areas of mechanical coating damage. An experimental fouling-release system containing Selektope still showed resistance to barnacle settlement where the coating was damaged.
entries.relevance_reason: maps directly onto the SPC vs FRC selection logic and risk assessment for warm-water, long-idle routes; note that it is a vendor white paper

entries.title: IMO MEPC 84 agrees to manage ship biofouling through a standalone mandatory instrument
entries.summary: MEPC 84 (27 April to 1 May, London) agreed to develop a standalone, legally binding instrument for the control and management of ships' biofouling to minimise the transfer of invasive aquatic species, with follow-up work assigned to the PPR Sub-Committee.
entries.relevance_reason: a mandatory convention will directly affect antifouling coating selection, inspection and cleaning requirements, and compliance costs on every route

entries.title: HullPIC 2026: industry calls for greater transparency in hull performance data
entries.summary: The 11th HullPIC was held in Italy with more than 90 shipowners, service providers, coating manufacturers and experts attending; participants including Jotun argued that linking hull performance measurement with biofouling management is a core industry challenge, and that standardised, comparable performance claims based on methods such as ISO 19030 are needed.
entries.relevance_reason: once performance claim conventions are unified, cross-comparisons between commercial coatings will become more reliable

entries.title: 8th Marine Fouling Protection Technology Symposium held in Xiamen
entries.summary: The Marine Fouling Protection Technology Committee of the Chinese Society for Corrosion and Protection held the symposium in Xiamen on 17–19 April, with more than 200 participants, 16 plenary talks and 48 parallel-session talks covering the engineering of antifouling coatings, molecular design of new antifouling materials, intelligent protection, and test and evaluation methods; the 9th edition is scheduled for 2027, hosted by Harbin Engineering University.
entries.relevance_reason: reflects the overall direction of domestic antifouling formulation research and evaluation methods

entries.title: Singapore's MPA selects six partners for in-port underwater hull inspection and cleaning innovation trials
entries.summary: The MPA selected Alicia Bots, C-Leanship, Neptune Robotics, Oceanis Robotics, RINA and SEAHI Robotics from 19 proposals submitted by 36 companies, with nearly S$3.7 million in R&D co-funding from the MINT fund; the trials will run for 18 months from the second half of 2026, focusing on complex areas such as propellers, rudders and sea chests, operations in strong currents, and debris collection requirements.

entries.title: Kawasaki Kisen tug BISAN MARU launched, becoming Japan's first tug fitted with an ultrasonic hull antifouling system
entries.summary: Ordered by SEAGATE, the vessel is fitted with both a biofuel blending unit and an ultrasonic antifouling system from M-SAT, which uses ultrasound to suppress marine growth; the system was originally developed for a hybrid-electric tug to be delivered in 2027 and is being validated in service on this vessel first, with entry into service at Mizushima Port expected in August 2026.

entries.title: Neptune Robotics invests US$12 million in a Singapore manufacturing and R&D base
entries.summary: The company plans to expand its autonomous hull cleaning capacity fivefold, reaching 60 cleanings per day by 2027; the new base focuses on computer vision and machine learning, aiming for round-the-clock operation in low visibility and currents of up to 4 knots, with a service network currently covering 61 ports in Singapore and China.
entries.relevance_reason: expansion of a cleaning service provider; only an indirect influence on formulation choices
